# The Great Works

> An age of builders. The ancient wonders come cheaper and give more, monuments raise culture faster, and any capital can make a run at one. The Concord sits a little further off, to keep the clock honest.

**Play:** [Skirmish](https://tessera4x.com/#world=skirmish&seed=276767781&) · [Full game](https://tessera4x.com/#world=custom&seed=276767781&) · or download [mod.json](mod.json)  
**Author:** Tessera4X · **Changes:** 17
<!-- head:end -->

## How it plays

Seven ancient and classical wonders cost 20–31% less, and four of them give
more: Stonehenge +5 culture, the Temple of Artemis +4 food, the Pyramids
+2 culture and the Hanging Gardens +6 food. Monuments cost 40 and give
3 culture, and Mining, Masonry and Bronze Working come cheaper.

The question is which wonder to go for, and whether you can hold the capital
that builds it. The Concord costs 480 instead of 400, because the extra
culture brings it into reach sooner.

## Balance Lab

48 machine-only skirmishes, the Lab's own worlds (a Tiny map, three civilizations, 60 turns), each played twice: by the game's own rules and by this mod. Run on Tessera4X 1.3.

| | Game's own rules | This mod |
|---|---|---|
| Games ended on score at the final turn | 48 of 48 | 48 of 48 |
| Cities per civilization at the end | 6.1 | 6.3 |
| Score per civilization | 343 | 353 |
| Soldiers raised per game | 61.2 | 62.6 |
| Wonders standing per game | 3.5 | 3.8 |
| Civilizations knocked out | 1 of 144 | 0 of 144 |
| Of the seven cheaper wonders, standing per game | 2.3 | 2.4 |
| Monuments standing per game | 7.9 | 8.9 |

The machine builds the seven cheaper wonders about as often as it does by the game's own rules: a lower price doesn't change what rivals choose to build. The race is there for a player who runs it.
